hints.content: **Reflective (or line) symmetry** means that we can reflect a figure across a line, and the figure will remain unchanged.

##Reflection over $x=0$

Under this transformation, some points on the triangle map to another point which is no longer on the triangle. The triangle is *not symmetric* over this line.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: An equilateral triangle mapped onto a coordinate plane. The x- y-coordinate plane scales by ones. The equilateral triangle has a point at about negative six, negative three, a point at about one half, seven, and a point at six, negative four. The equation x equals zero is graphed on the coordinate plane. Dotted lines show the points of the triangle when reflected over the graphed line.

hints.content:
##Reflection over $y=-\dfrac{2}{3}x$

This line goes through the center of the triangle and one of the corner points $(6,-4)$. 

Under this transformation, each point on the triangle maps to another point which is also on the triangle. The triangle is *symmetric* over this line.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: An equilateral triangle mapped onto a coordinate plane. The x- y-coordinate plane scales by ones. The equilateral triangle has a point at about negative six, negative three, a point at about one half, seven, and a point at six, negative four. The equation y equals negative two thirds x is graphed on the coordinate plane.  A line is graphed that shows the points of the triangle when reflected over the graphed line.

hints.content:
The symmetries that apply to the triangle are:

Symmetry | Applies to the figure?
:- | :-:
Reflective symmetry over the line $x=0$ | No
Reflective symmetry over the line $y=-\dfrac{2}{3}x$ | Yes
